G8602.definition:
1.  to look aside, take a side look  , (Aristophanes Comicus); π. θατέρῳ (i.e. ὀφθαλμῷ);  to look suspiciously   with one eye, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2.  to see wrong  , (Lucian) (ML)

G8603.definition:
1.  a message transmitted   by beacons, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2.  an order, command  , ἀπὸ παραγγέλματος  by word of command  , (Thucydides) 
3.  an instruction, precept  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8606.definition:
1.  a pattern   or  model   of the thing to be executed, Lat.  exemplar , an architect's  plan  , (Herdotus Historicus); a sculptor's or painter's  model  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  a precedent, example  , (Thucydides); ἐπὶ παραδείγματος by way of  example  , (Aeschines Orator) 
3.  an example  , i. e.  a lesson   or  warning  , π. ἔχειν τινός to take  a lesson   from another, (Thucydides); τὸ σὸν π. ἔχων (Sophocles Tragicus); ζῶντά τινα τοῖς λοιποῖς π. ποιεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
4.  an argument, proof from example  , (Thucydides) 
5.  the model   or  copy   of an existing thing, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8607.gloss: to hold forth as an example
G8607.definition:
1.  to exhibit side by side  : generally,  to exhibit, bring forward  , in Mid., (Demosthenes Orator) 
2.  to represent   as so and so, π. τινὰ οὐκ ὄντα (Polybius Historicus): also in bad sense, like παραδειγματίζω, (Plutarch) 
3.  to exhibit and hand over  , τί τινι (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8608.definition: to do an incredible thing; render notorious

G8609.definition: a running beside   or  over, traversing  , (Plutarch); ἐν παραδρομῇ  cursorily  , (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G8611.definition: to heat to excess  :—;Pass., aor1  participle  παραθερμανθείς, of a man  become quarrelsome   in his cups, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8612.definition: juxta-position, neighbourhood  , (Polybius Historicus); ἐκ παραθέσεως on  comparison  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8614.definition:
1.  to take away from beside, withdraw, remove  , (Euripides):—; with  genitive   partitive   to take away part of   a thing, (Euripides):—;Pass., παρῃρημένοι τὰ ὅπλα  having   their arms taken from them, (Thucydides) 
2. π. ἀρὰν εἰς παῖδα  to draw aside   the curse on thy son's head, (Euripides) 
3. Mid.  to draw over to one's own side, seduce, detach  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  to take away  , (Xenophon Historicus): Mid., παραιρεῖσθαι τὴν θρασύτητα  to lessen, damp   it, (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. generally,  to take away from, steal away from  , τί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8615.definition: Dep.  to be seated beside   or  near   another, with  dative , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G8617.definition:
1. Dep. 
2.  to order   one  to   do a thing,  advise, prescribe  , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; π. ταῦτα  to give   this  advice  , (Plato Philosophus);—;also, π. τινι, with  infinitive , (Plato Philosophus) 
3.  to exhort  , τοιαῦτα παρακελευσάμενος  having delivered   this  address  , (Thucydides):—; absolute   to encourage one another by shouting  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. παρακεκέλευστο in  passive  sense,  orders had been given  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8621.definition:
1.  to strike aside: to disappoint, mislead  , (Plato Philosophus):—;Pass.  to be led astray, go wrong  , (Plato Philosophus):—;so also in Mid., (Isocrates Orator) 
2. in Mid. also,  to strike away from oneself, parry  , (Plutarch) (ML)

G8624.definition:
1.  to make things alternate, to transpose  , (Plato Philosophus) 
2.  to change   or  alter a little  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. of Place,  to pass by, go past, elude  , (Xenophon Historicus):—;  to get rid of  , (Plutarch) 
4.  to go beyond, exceed   in point of time, (Plutarch) 
5.  intransitive   to pass by one another, to overlap  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
6.  to differ, vary  , (Herdotus Historicus):—; impersonal , οὐ σμικρὸν παραλλάττει  it makes   no small  difference  , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. π. τοῦ σκοποῦ  to go aside from   the mark, (Plato Philosophus) 
8.  to deviate from the course, to be liable to deviation  , (Plato Philosophus); λόγοι παραλλάσσοντες  delirious  , (Euripides) 
9.  to slip aside   or  away  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8625.definition: a loosening by the side: paralysis, palsy  , (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8626.definition: to spend amiss, to waste, squander  , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass., of persons,  to be sacrificed uselessly  , 3rd  plural  aor1 παραναλώθησαν (Plutarch) (ML)

G8627.definition:
1.  acting contrary to law, lawless  , (Euripides) 
2. of things,  contrary to law, unlawful  , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.:—; adverb , παρανόμως,  illegally  , (Thucydides) 
3. in attic law, παράνομα γράφειν, εἰπεῖν to propose an  illegal measure  , (Demosthenes Orator); παρανόμων γράφεσθαί τινα to indict one  for proposing such a measure  , (Demosthenes Orator): the indictment itself was παρανόμων γραφή (Aeschines Orator):—;in  superlative , παρανομώτατα γεγραφότα (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G8629.definition: a knife worn beside the sword, a dirk  , (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8630.definition:
1.  altogether, absolutely  , generally with Art., τὸ π. (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;with a  negative , τὸ π. οὐδέν not  at all  , (Herdotus Historicus); οὔκ εἰμι τὸ π. ἄθεος (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in reckoning, ἐπὶ διηκόσια τὸ παράπαν up to two hundred  altogether  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8631.definition: that which is spread before   a thing,  a hanging curtain  , (Herdotus Historicus):—; metaphorically   a screen, cover  , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8634.definition: a falling beside;   κατὰ τὴν π. τινος in  the course   of an action, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8635.definition: to throw beside  :  metaphorically   to run the risk   of doing a thing, with  participle , π. λαμβάνων (Sophocles Tragicus):  to throw aside, reject  , [  variant  dates Anthology Palantina   (ML)

G8637.definition: to pass over in silence  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8638.definition:
1.  a putting aside   or  away, banishing, relegatio  , (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2.  a setting out   things  for sale, retail-trade  , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3.  παρίσταμαι);  intransitive   a being beside  : 
4.  a position   or  post near   a king, (Xenophon Historicus) 
5.  presence of mind, courage  , (Polybius Historicus): also,  desperation  , (Polybius Historicus) 
6. as law-term,  a small money deposit   on entering law-suits, (Isaeus Orator) (ML)

G8641.definition:
1.  to place side by side, draw up in battle-order  , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Mid.  to draw up one's men in battle-order  , (Xenophon Historicus); so of ships, (Thucydides):—;Mid. and Pass.  to be drawn up along  , παρατετάχατο παρὰ τὴν ἀκτήν (Herdotus Historicus); ἑκατέρωθεν παρατεταγμένοι (Thucydides); so, παρετάξαντο ἀλλήλοις (Xenophon Historicus):  absolute , παρατεταγμένοι or παραταξάμενοι  in order of battle  , (Thucydides) 
2. in Mid. and Pass., also,  to stand prepared  , παρατετάχθαι πρὸς τὸ ἀποκρίνεσθαι (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8642.definition:
1.  to run by   or  past  , (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  to outrun, overtake  , (Iliad by Homer): π. τὰ τότε κακά  to go beyond, exceed   them, (Euripides) 
3.  to run through   or  over, run across   (a space of ground expressed or implied), (Xenophon Historicus) 
4.  to run over  , i. e.  treat in a cursory way  , (Isocrates Orator):—;  to slight, neglect  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
5.  to escape unnoticed  , τινά (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8645.definition:
1.  to sit constantly beside, attend constantly, be always near  , Lat.  assidere , with  dative , (Euripides) 
2. of judges,  to be an assessor  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8647.definition: to stretch out in line  , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8649.definition:
1. as  preposition , 
2. with  genitive  loci,  outside, before  , παρὲκ λιμένος (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ὁδοῦ  out of   the road, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. like χωρίς,  besides, except, exclusive of  , παρὲξ τοῦ ἀργύρου (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. with  accusative   out by the side of, along side of  , παρὲξ ἅλα (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ τὴν νῆσον  away from   the island, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ δοῦρα  out of the way of   spears, (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲκ νόον  out of   sense and reason, foolishly, (Iliad by Homer); παρὲξ Ἀχιλῆα  without the knowledge of   Achilles, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. as  adverb , 
6. of Place,  out beside  , στῆ δὲ παρέξ  hard by  , (Iliad by Homer); νῆχε παρέξ was swimming  out along shore  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
7.  metaphorically   beside the mark  , παρὲξ ἀγορεύειν (Iliad by Homer) 
8. ἄλλα παρὲξ μεμνώμεθα let us talk  of something else  , (Odyssey by Homer); παρὲξ ἢ ὅσον  except   so long as, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8651.definition: marks of virginity; tokens of virginity

G8653.definition:
παρ-ιστάνω , see: παρίστημι.
  παρ-ίστημι  
 [in LXX for עָמַד, etc. ;] 
__I. Transitive verb. in present tense., imperfect., future tense., 1 aorist.; 
 __1.  to place beside, present, provide : with accusative,  Act.9:41 23:24 ,  2Co.4:14 ,  Col.1:28 ; with accusative and dative,  Mat.26:53 ,  Luk.2:22 ,  Act.1:3 23:33 ,  1Co.8:8 ; before accusative pred.,  Rom.6:13, 16  (late pres., παριστάνετε),  Rom.6:19 12:1 ,  2Co.11:2 ,  Eph.5:27 ,  Col.1:22 ,  2Ti.2:15 . 
 __2. to present to the mind (cl.) : by argument, to prove (Xen., FlJ, al.), with accusative,  Act.24:13.  
 __II. Intransitive. in  perfect., pluperfect., 2 aorist.; 
 __1.  to stand by or beside one  : with dative of person(s),  Act.1:10 9:39 23:2 27:23 ; ptcp.,  Mrk.14:47, 69-70 15:35, 39   Jhn.18:22 19:26 . 
 __2.  to appear : with nom. pred., before ἐνώπιον,  Act.4:10;  with dative of person(s),  Act.27:24;  so fut. mid. (of. LS, see word, B, ii, 2),  Rom.14:10.  
 __3.  to be at hand, be present, have come :  Act.4:26  (LXX); of servants in attendance, ἐνώπιον τ. θεοῦ,  Luk.1:19;  absol., οἱ παρεστῶτες,  Luk.19:24;  before αὐτῷ,  Act.23:2 , 4; of time,  Mrk.4:29  
 __4.  to stand by for help or defence  (Hom., Dem., Xen., al.): with dative of person(s),  Rom.16:2 ,  2Ti.4:17 .†
 (AS)

G8654.definition:
1.  to pass by  , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. with  accusative   to go past  , (Lucian) (ML)

G8657.definition:
1.  to behave ill at wine, play drunken tricks  , (Isaeus Orator) 
2.  to act like a drunken man  , (Plutarch); παροινήσας  in a drunken fit  , (Plato Philosophus) 
3.  transitive   to treat with drunken violence  :—; Pass.  to be so treated  , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8659.definition:
1.  to look at by the way, notice, remark  , (Xenophon Historicus); τί τινι something in one, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2.  to overlook, disregard, neglect  , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
3.  to see amiss, see wrong  , (Plato Philosophus) 
4.  to look sideways  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8662.definition:
1.  a peg   on which to hang clothes, arms, etc., (Homer), etc.; ἀπὸ πασσαλόφι ζυγὸν ᾕρεον (Iliad by Homer); ἀπὸ πασσάλου αἴνυτο τόξον (Odyssey by Homer); ἐκ πασσαλόφι κρέμασεν φόρμιγγα (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  a gag  , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8663.definition:
1.  to sprinkle  , φάρμακα πάσσων  laying   salves  upon   a wound, (Iliad by Homer): —;with  genitive   partitive , πάσσε ἁλός  sprinkle some   salt, (Iliad by Homer) 
2.  to besprinkle  , χρυσῶι, ῥόδοις π. τινά (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3.  metaphorically   to embroider, broider  , (Iliad by Homer); π. ἀέθλους  to work   battles  in embroidery  , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8670.definition:
1.  of   or  belonging to one's father  , Lat.  patrius , (Pindar), etc. 
2. = πατρικός,  derived from one's fathers, hereditary  , οἱπ. θεοί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.: —; τὰ πάτρια, Lat.  instituta majorum , κατὰ τὰ πάτρια (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.; rarely in  singular , τὸ πάτριον παρείς neglecting  the rule of our fathers  , (Thucydides) Cf. πατρῷος. (ML)

G8672.definition: hoar-frost, rime  , Lat.  pruina , (Odyssey by Homer):  metaphorically , κουροβόρος π.  the clotted blood   of the eaten children, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8673.definition:
1.  thickness  , (Odyssey by Homer):—;  absolute , πάχος  in thickness  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. π. σαρκός  stoutness  , (Euripides) (ML)

G8674.definition:
1.  thick, stout  , (Homer):—; later,  stout, fat  , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of things,  thick, massive  , (Homer):—; adverb  -έως,  roughly  , of stating or arguing, (Aristotle Philosopher); παχύτερον or -έρως, (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of liquids,  thick, curdled, clotted  , (Iliad by Homer) 
4. οἱ παχέες  the men of substance, the wealthy class  , (Herdotus Historicus); τοὺς παχεῖς καὶ πλουσίους (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. in [  variant  dates Comica Adespota   and Prose,  thick-witted, gross, dull, stupid  , like Lat.  pinguis, crassus , [  variant  dates Comica Adespota   
6.  comparative  παχύτερος, sup. -ύτατος:—;irregular  comparative  πάσσων, ον, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Sup. πάχιστος, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8675.definition:
1.  to bind with fetters, to bind fast, make fast  , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2.  to shackle, trammel, constrain  , (Homer); with  infinitive   to constrain   one to do a thing, (Homer) (ML)

G8676.definition:
a plain   or  flat  , and collectively  a plain flat open country  , (Homer), etc. 
 (ML)

G8677.definition:
1.  on foot  , πεζοί  fighters on foot  , opposite to horsemen, (Homer):—;also  on land, going by land  , opposite to sea-faring, (Homer):—;so, ὁ πεζὸς στρατός, or ὁ πεζός alone, sometimes  foot-soldiery, infantry  , opposite to cavalry  ἡ ἵππος); (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. ὁ πεζός, also,  a land-force   or  army  , opposite to a naval force, (Herdotus Historicus); so, τὸ πεζόν (Herdotus Historicus); στρατιὰ καὶ ναυτικὴ καὶ πεζή (Thucydides); τὰ πεζὰ κράτιστοι strongest  by land  , (Thucydides) 
3. of animals,  land  , as opposite to birds and fishes, τὰ π. καὶ τὰ πτηνά  beasts   and birds, (Plato Philosophus) 
4.  metaphorically  of language,  not rising above the ground, prosaic  , (Lucian) 
5.  dative   feminine  πεζῇ (entry ὁδῷ); as  adverb ,  on foot  , (Xenophon Historicus) 
6.  by land  , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8680.definition: a pirate  , Lat.  pirata , i. e.  one who attacks   ships, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8681.definition:
1.  near, hard by, close  , with  genitive , (Odyssey by Homer) 
3.  absolute , χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [  variant  dates Tragica Adespota   
4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες);  one's neighbours  , (Thucydides), etc.: hence  one's fellow-creatures, all men  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8683.definition: to hew   or  shape with an axe  , Lat.  dolare , (Odyssey by Homer) (in epic aor1 πελέκκησε), (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G8685.definition:
1.  an axe   for felling trees, with two edges, opposite to the ἡμιπέλεκκον, (Homer) 
2.  a sacrificial axe  , (Homer)—;That it was not, properly,  a battle axe   appears from the phrase, οὐ δόρασι μάχεσθαι, ἀλλὰ καὶ πελέκεσι to fight not with spears only, but with  common axes  , i. e. to the last, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. in (Theophrastus Philosophus) Char., πέλεκυς as a child's nickname seems to mean  a sharp blade.   (ML)

G8688.definition: one who bears a light shield   πέλτη); instead of the heavy ὅπλον,  a targeteer  , Lat.  cetratus , (Euripides), etc. The peltasts held a place between the ὁπλῖται and ψιλοί. (ML)

G8689.definition:
1.  a small light shield   of leather  without a rim   ἴτυς);  a target  , Lat.  cetra , originally used by the Thracians, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2.  a body of   πελτασταί, (Euripides) 
3.  a horse's ornament  , (Euripides) 
4. = παλτόν,  a shaft, pole  , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8690.definition: a kind of  axe  , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8691.definition: any kind of dressed food;   but mostly in  plural ,  pastry, cakes, sweetmeats  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8692.definition: of   or  for mourning, mournful  :—; adverb , πενθικῶς ἔχειν τινός to be in  mourning   for a person, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8694.definition:
1. Dep., used in  present  and  imperfect  : 
2.  intransitive   to work for one's daily bread  ; generally,  to toil, work, labour  , (Homer) 
3.  to be poor   or  needy  ,  Solon  , (Euripides), etc. 
4. with  genitive   to be poor in, have need of  , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5.  transitive   to work at, prepare, get ready  , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8695.definition:
1.  five years old  , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of Time,  lasting five years  , (Thucydides):—;  neuter   adverb  πεντάετες,  for five years  , (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

G8696.definition: five cubits long   or  broad  , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)
